title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 5th District
area: Minneapolis and surrounding Hennepin County suburbs, including Saint Louis Park, Richfield and parts of Bloomington and Brooklyn Park.

context.text: Incumbent Ilhan Omar (D) won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.7% of the vote against four challengers. John Nagel won the Republican primary with 52.2% against three challengers. DeVelle Jackson is running as an independent.

candidates.name: Ilhan Omar
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.7% of the vote.

summary.text: Ilhan Omar is the Democratic incumbent for Minnesota's 5th Congressional District, which includes Minneapolis and surrounding suburbs. A Somali-born former refugee, she worked as a community educator and policy aide before serving in the Minnesota House from 2017 to 2019, and was first elected to Congress in 2018. She serves on the House Budget and Education and Workforce committees and is Deputy Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

background.text: Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, on October 4, 1982; her family fled the civil war when she was eight and spent four years in a refugee camp in Kenya before coming to the United States.
Moved to Minneapolis with her family in 1997, according to her House website.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international studies from North Dakota State University in 2011.

Worked as a community educator at the University of Minnesota, a Policy Fellow at the Humphrey School of Public Affairs, and a Senior Policy Aide for the Minneapolis City Council before running for office.
Elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives (District 60B) in 2016, defeating incumbent Phyllis Kahn in the Democratic primary; served from 2017 to 2019.

Elected to the U.S. House on November 6, 2018, defeating Jennifer Zielinski (R) 78.0% to 21.7% in the open seat; sworn in January 2019, she was the first Somali-American and first African refugee in Congress and, with Rashida Tlaib, one of the first two Muslim women elected to Congress.

Serves on the House Budget Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee (Workforce Protections Subcommittee and the Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Subcommittee); Deputy Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and Vice Chair of the Medicare for All Caucus.

priorities.text: Abolish U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), citing deaths in ICE custody and due-process concerns in immigration courts.

Lower prescription drug costs, cap child care costs at 7% of income, expand rental assistance, provide $20,000 in down-payment assistance for first-time homebuyers, and make college and trade school tuition-free.
End what she calls 'forever wars' and require congressional authorization for military action, prioritizing diplomacy and human rights in foreign policy.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing ICE rather than expanding immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: There is no reforming an agency that will ignore the Constitution and kill Americans and prevent any meaningful investigation into their deaths. ICE must be abolished.

positions.summary: Supports replacing for-profit health insurance with Medicare for All.
positions.quote: replacing for-profit health insurance with Medicare For All

positions.summary: Supports a wealth tax on billionaires as part of the Progressive Caucus agenda she helps advance.
Backs capping child care costs at 7% of household income.
positions.quote: cap child care costs at 7% of income

positions.summary: Supports environmental justice initiatives as part of addressing the climate crisis.
Supports expanding rental assistance to address housing costs.

record.text: Serves on the House Budget Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee in the 119th Congress; is the lead Democrat on the Workforce Protections Subcommittee.
Serves as Deputy Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
Introduced the Make ICE Pay Act, announced September 17, 2026, following 'Operation Metro Surge' immigration enforcement activity in Minnesota.
Spoke at a September 22, 2026 House Oversight and Government Reform Committee hearing on deaths in DHS custody, alongside family members of people who died during immigration enforcement encounters.

candidates.name: John Nagel
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 52.2% of the vote.

summary.text: John Nagel is the Republican nominee in Minnesota's 5th Congressional District. A retired Minnesota State Patrol field lieutenant, he spent roughly 30 years with the patrol and, according to his campaign website, is running on public safety, immigration enforcement and lower federal spending.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a lifelong resident of Saint Louis Park, Minnesota, and lives in the home his grandfather built.
Studied criminal justice at the University of St. Thomas, where he interned with the Edina Police Department and rode along with Saint Louis Park officers.

Entered the Minnesota State Patrol Academy in 1981 and served about 30 years as a state trooper, patrolling Hennepin County, working as a safety consultant for the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, and serving on the Governor's security detail.

Rose to Sergeant at the State Patrol Training Academy, overseeing traffic safety programs, and retired as a Field Lieutenant in 2011; his campaign site lists the State Patrol's Meritorious Service Award and an Employee of the Year honor.

After retiring, taught defensive driving and college courses on terrorism and world governments, served on the Minnesota Twins security team, and became a Minnesota DNR youth firearm instructor, according to his campaign website.
Says he has been married to Connie since 1988 and has two children and a grandchild.

priorities.text: Cut federal spending and taxes, and reduce what he calls government waste and intrusiveness.
Support law enforcement funding and back Attorney General efforts against violent crime.
Secure the U.S.-Mexico border and support the Trump administration's border enforcement approach.

positions.summary: Supports strengthening border security and immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will fight to make sure our border is locked down so tightly that Democrats can never tear it open again.

positions.summary: Supports increased funding and support for police.
positions.quote: our men and women in blue receive the funding and support they deserve

positions.summary: Campaigns on cutting taxes and reducing federal spending rather than raising taxes.
positions.quote: I will cut taxes, fight inflation, eliminate fraud and waste, and restore accountability in Washington.

positions.summary: Criticizes current school curricula and calls for schools to focus on 'the basics,' though does not explicitly call for voucher or charter funding on his campaign site.
positions.quote: We need classrooms that focus on learning, not indoctrination.

positions.summary: States he will 'never tolerate Jew-hatred in any form' and frames support for Israel-related positions as a campaign theme, in contrast to Rep. Omar.
positions.quote: I will never tolerate Jew-hatred in any form and will always put people before politics.

candidates.name: DeVelle Jackson

summary.text: DeVelle Jackson is an independent candidate in Minnesota's 5th Congressional District with a background in construction and field engineering. He describes himself as an independent running to challenge the two-party system, and has prepared for law school.

background.text: Graduated from Mounds View High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities.
Career experience includes construction, field engineering and construction superintendent roles.
Says he has volunteered as a docent with The King Center for four years and has prepared for law school.

priorities.text: Reduce the two-party system's control over political access, arguing elected officials should answer to voters rather than party establishments.

Strengthen privacy and data-rights protections against government and corporate surveillance, including limits on facial recognition, geofencing, and government purchase of personal data to bypass warrant requirements.
Pair direct affordability relief with policies to expand housing supply, domestic production, and job training rather than relief alone.

positions.summary: Supports building more housing as part of an affordability agenda focused on expanding supply.
positions.quote: That means making it easier to build, produce, hire, train, and compete while ensuring working people share in the value they create.

candidates.researchNotes: Jackson completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website, prior officeholding, or additional press coverage was found.
